body:
The two-phase erasure machine (§11, §29) is the most legally consequential subsystem in the
store, and no surface a person can reach exists for any of it: no way to list what is slated, no
CLI verb to erase, no way to read a receipt without an embedding script. The vision doc's
compliance story founders on exactly this — the DPO cannot run the pitch.

Build three verbs, each a transcription of a ground read or an existing gateway call — NO new
erasure semantics:
- `loam slate list` — each active slate: who asked, when, the deadline, the condemned set's
  size and frozen content address (§29.1's record, printed).
- `loam erase <deltaId> --reason <text>` — wraps the existing gateway.erase. --reason is
  REQUIRED: the receipt records why, and an erasure without a stated reason is a receipt made
  less honest. Prints the tombstone id on success.
- `loam tombstones list` (and `loam tombstones show <id>`) — the per-id receipts: THAT an
  id was forgotten, by whom, when, the reason — never what. Vocabulary matters here: in the
  codebase and §29.6 a GRAVEYARD is the cut-event record (Gateway.graveyards() — container,
  version, memberCount, cutAt; no per-id reason), and a single gateway.erase mints only a
  TOMBSTONE. The reader for these verbs is survivingTombstones (src/gateway/erase.ts).
  §29.6 cut records are out of this ticket's scope — a graveyard reader can follow when the
  slate flow gets its own surface.

Erasure discipline applies in full. This ticket widens NO purge: the verb invokes the existing
single-delta gateway.erase, and the PR must state in one line that nothing can now be deleted
that could not before. Every rail is two-sided (target gone AND a named bystander survives).
Tests erase only inside their own mkdtempSync fixtures — never a real home, never
demos/village/homes/.

Acceptance criteria — all via CLI tests in mkdtemp homes:
(a) `loam slate list` on a store with an active slate prints who/when/deadline and the frozen
    set's address; with no slates it says so plainly (two-sided). Verify: new test
    test/cli/erasure-verbs.test.ts.
(b) `loam erase <id> --reason r` removes the bytes at every local tier and prints the receipt
    id; a named bystander delta still resolves after (two-sided). Verify: same file.
(c) `loam erase <id>` without --reason refuses and names the missing flag; nothing is erased
    by the refused call (two-sided). Verify: same file.
(d) `loam tombstones show` prints who/when/reason and does NOT contain the erased content's
    bytes (the receipt remembers that, never what). Verify: same file.

Merge tier — split honestly, land as TWO PRs. The readers (`slate list`, `tombstones
list/show`) are the report-honesty side of the erasure split (Myk, 2026-07-25): self-merge on
the ordinary bar. `loam erase` is an ACTION surface — a new user-reachable capability, which
the merge-by-risk test routes to Myk even though it widens no purge (it wraps the existing
operator-only single-delta gateway.erase; nothing becomes deletable that an embedding script
could not already delete — the PR states this in one line). Land the readers first,
self-merged; the erase verb second, Myk's merge.
title: Erasure gets a CLI — slate list, erase, and the tombstone reader
